# 2 Baruch Chapter 21 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**21:1** And I went forth and sat in a cave in the valley of Kidron, and I fasted there seven days.

**21:2** And after seven days I lifted up my eyes toward heaven, opened my mouth, and said:

**21:3** O Lord my God, you who called the beginning into being before the ages, before whom the ages stand, and in whose hand is the passing of all time —

**21:4** You whose throne stands in heights beyond all reckoning, and whose glory is beyond all searching out —

**21:5** Before whom the armies of the angels stand trembling, serving in fear and fire before your glory —

**21:6** You who have no beginning and no end; who upheld the living by your word and summoned the dead by your command —

**21:7** You who appointed the number of the living and fixed the limits of the dead; who does not permit the kings to transgress your commandments —

**21:8** You who remember all things and forget nothing among all that has been created —

**21:9** Hear, O Lord, my prayer, and give heed to my supplication.

**21:10** For we are, all of us, nothing compared to you; we are as though we did not exist, and like a drop from a bucket.

**21:11** We pass away like morning mist, and our strength is as vapor.

**21:12** In your goodness are ordered our days, and in the compassion of your right hand are numbered our years.

**21:13** For the Most High is great, and the Mighty One is powerful; and he has not forgotten even one among the sons of men.

**21:14** O Lord, you have heard the prayer of those who have fallen asleep, and you are to be feared before the departed.

**21:15** Was it not written in former times by the mouth of the prophets: Behold, the days are coming when the Most High will visit the world which he made?

**21:16** And he will call to account those who have transgressed his commandment; he will judge the living by means of the dead, and will repay those who have transgressed with the fruits of their transgression.

**21:17** And he will raise up those who were sleeping in the dust, and will bring forth the living ones who have waited for him, and will bring into the treasury those who were sealed, so that they may enter their rest.

**21:18** And then he will destroy those who have corrupted themselves and will deliver those who have defiled themselves to the fire.

**21:19** And when he has subjected everything corruptible, renewed the age, and revived those who slept in hope of him —

**21:20** Then shall his rest come.

**21:21** For you alone are able to do this, and so I speak before you.

**21:22** For your furnace is full, and the abundance of your compassion is being withheld from those who live now.

**21:23** Yet if you had compassion on those who are now alive, and if you hastened your times and shortened the measure of the ages —

**21:24** You would not have left your treasury empty, and the coming age would not have been so long delayed.

**21:25** For great is your strength, O Lord, and great is your glory; great is your beauty, and great is your grace, and great is your compassion. Amen, amen.

**21:26** And after these things I sat there seven more days.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering of Baruch's great intercessory prayer. The structure rehearses God's sovereignty over time and death as the basis for Baruch's plea to hasten the end. Key decisions: "treasury of souls" implied in v.17 (EMET/LOGOS); "fallen asleep" retained for the dead (v.14) over PNEUMA's "already died"; "sons of men" preserved (v.13) as a Semitic idiom with theological resonance.*
